**4. The checker stall: what the CLI leaves the camera in.**

Runs. Each row is a power cycle, the step named, then a traced checker connect (`stream -n 3`, default flags unless noted). Results from the checker's log. [measured]

| run | step before the checker | power cycle between | checker result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rep1 | `slots flash a` (stock 1.3.0.0, verified) | no | 0x4e, 0x36, 0x37 and 0x3c OK; stall OUT 0x56 `01` |
| rep2 | same write | yes, 10 s | connected, streamed |
| rep3 | same write, `--no-verify` | no | stall OUT 0x56 `01` |
| rep4 | `slots list` only | no | stall OUT 0x56 `01` |
| expB | replay of rep4's 14 OUT transfers, no reads | no | Pro init chosen (first 0x4e byte 0xb8); stall OUT 0x55 `17 00` |
| expD | replay of OUT 0 to 6 | no | Pro init; stall OUT 0x55 `17 00` |
| expE | replay of OUT 0 only (the 2-byte 0x52 probe) | no | connected, streamed |
| expF | replay of OUT 0 to 3 | no | classic init; stall OUT 0x56 `01` |
| expG | replay of OUT 1 only (the 18-byte 0x52 packet) | no | classic init; stall OUT 0x56 `01` |
| expH | as expG, token bytes zeroed | no | packet refused (STALL); connected, streamed |
| expJ | compact-fps 5 s, no CLI | no | connected, streamed |
| expK | `slots flash a` (copy form 1.3.0.8) | yes, 10 s | stall OUT 0x37 `01 00 00 00` |
| expK2 | no CLI step, copy form on bank A | yes, 10 s | stall OUT 0x37 `01 00 00 00` (head `01 03 00 08`) |
| 0.9.1.0 | `slots list` after the 0.9.1.0 write | yes, then a series | stall OUT 0x56 three times (`--no-opzero`); after a cycle, connected |

The replays send the transfers of the CLI's own `slots list` trace (`trace/raw-replay.mjs`), with the same bytes and order and the same timeouts, then release and close the interface. The 14 transfers were, in order: 0x52 `05 00` (stalls), 0x52 18 B (accepted), 0x52 `01 00`, 0x55 `01 00`, 0x55 `14 00` (stalls), 0x55 `11 00` (stalls), 0x55 `0a 00`, 0x5a `00 00 7c 00 00 00`, 0x52 18 B ×5, 0x52 `00 00`. [measured]

What the CLI leaves. In every CLI trace (write, write without read-back, list): the stall-prone window setup above, then the reads, then `releaseInterface 0` and `close`, so the CLI closes the device. A write adds the commit (0x51, 20 s timeout, the transfer checksum; `cc 5e` for the stock 1.3.0.0 image), then the status read (IN 0x35, four bytes, 0), then the read-back (IN 0x4f, 64 B). The CLI sends no SetOperationMode (0x3C) and no SetImageProcessingMode (0x3E) in any of the four CLI traces, so no stream is left running. The camera's mode after the CLI was not read. [measured]

The token. The 18-byte payload is `05 00 53 16 10 31 80 dd 00 b7 4a f9 e4 17 c5 94 be d4`, which is `authPayload(0x05, OLD_FW_UNLOCK_TOKEN)` (`packages/core/src/profiles/legacy-auth.ts`, lines 129 to 146). The 2-byte form `05 00` is refused on the first try in every trace, and the 18-byte form is then accepted. The checker's init decision is in `e2e/lib/bench/seek-fps/camera.ts`: `usesCompactProInit` (line 111) takes the Pro init when the first byte of the 8-byte GetFirmwareInfo reply is 4 or more, and `readFirmwareHead` (line 124) keeps the first non-zero byte. [source]

Mechanism.
- [measured] The accepted token packet is the trigger. The packet alone (expG) makes the next init stall; the same packet with the token zeroed (expH) is refused and does not; the 2-byte probe (expE) does nothing.
- [measured] A power cycle clears it (rep2, and the 0.9.1.0 series). The checker's own close after a stall, and a new open in a later process, did not (rep4, the 0.9.1.0 attempts, expB).
- [measured] The stalled requests are the checker's first init writes: OUT 0x56 `01` in the classic init, OUT 0x55 `17 00` in the Pro init (expB, expD).
- [measured] The 8-byte GetFirmwareInfo reply changes after the token. In a clean boot it is `01 03 00 00 4f 63 74 20` (version 1.3.0.0, "Oct 21 2014"). After the token it was `b8 2a 00 14 00 00 01 14` (expB, expD, and this was the first read, so the Pro path was taken), and `00 09 00 00 53 65 70 20` (expF, a different entry, which the checker retried). A first byte of `b8` (184) passes the test for a 4.x camera, so the checker reads a 1.3.0.0 as a 4.x Pro and runs the Pro init. [inferred] This is the checker misreading a changed reply, not a firmware-version change.
- [inferred] The token leaves a flag in the camera's vendor-request handling that lasts until the power cycle, and that flag refuses the classic init's 0x56 `01` and the Pro init's 0x55 `17 00`. The GetFirmwareInfo cursor's window bytes are a side effect. The firmware was not decoded to confirm either.
- [not established] A firmware request that re-locks without a power cycle. The CLI's last transfer, `52 00 00`, does not re-lock (expB ends with it and stalls).

The 0x37 stall is different. The copy image refuses OUT 0x37 with no CLI step before it (expK2), so the 1.3.0.8 image refuses `Startup with Operation=0` on a clean boot. The 1.3.0.0 image accepts it (rep1, rep3). So the op-5 stall of 42.37 and the copy stall of this section are firmware refusals of the default option, not a CLI effect. [measured on the copy image; the op-5 image was not re-run]

Recommended fix (not made; the owner decides).
1. Checker: choose the init from a GetFirmwareInfo reply that is consistent, not from one read's first byte. Read until two consecutive 8-byte replies agree and the major is 0 to 9; otherwise report the state. When an init request stalls, say the camera is unlocked by a slot command and needs a power cycle, not a bare stall.
2. Checker: `Startup with Operation=0` should be off for the 1.3.0.8 family, or the checker should retry without it on a 0x37 stall.
3. CLI: after any command that sends the unlock packet (`slots list`, `dump`, `flash`, `patch-fps`; the list sends it too), print that the camera stays unlocked until its next power cycle and that other tools will stall until then.
4. Firmware (FW-V1): a re-lock request, if one exists, would remove the power cycle. Look for it in the USB handler before deciding.

**5. End.**

- Restore: `FACTORY_IMAGE=/private/tmp/claude-501/agent-hw2/start-4m.bin node tools/jlink/jlink-runner.js flash-factory-4m-2` after a channel-1 cycle and an 8 s wait. `plan: 1 of 64 blocks differ -> 0x14050000 +0x10000`, attempt 1 verified, `DONE: the part reads back byte-identical` (`restore-1.log`). [measured]
- End dump: channel-1 cycle, 8 s, `dump-spifi-4m-halted`, copied to `end-4m.bin`: sha256 `50e900c23ff4bb7e0a5a30fc5879f6ed276289e43aeace2f9ab74eaec9b01d7d`. `cmp start-4m.bin end-4m.bin` printed nothing and exited 0. [measured]
- Normal fps after a channel-2 cycle and 10 s, checker default flags, reads 1 to 20 (`fps/end-normal-*.log`). Reads 1 to 12 are not settled: medians 16.2 to 32.1 per second, means 14.4 to 16.2 fps. Read by read, medians: 1: 17.84 20.63 27.04 16.66 17.98; 2: 25.33 27.81 26.95 30.25 26.66; 3: 31.79 30.07 23.64 17.89 17.83; 4: 19.92 25.75 27.68 31.49 27.27; 5: 32.05 24.03 19.00 18.55 16.54; 6: 18.05 18.45 29.00 24.08 20.86; 7: 18.97 18.14 26.50 17.92 23.24; 8: 16.24 19.15 26.19 27.67 28.48; 9: 27.39 31.94 26.18 26.76 16.33; 10: 29.14 30.55 30.78 19.01 27.55; 11: 27.46 18.40 17.37 20.56 25.02; 12: 19.02 28.58 22.27 27.21 28.86. Reads 13 to 20 are steady, medians 32.14 to 32.21, means 21.6 to 21.8 fps. Read 20: 32.18 32.18 32.19 32.18 32.21. [measured]

**Not measured or open.**
- The 42.27 first 0.9.1.0 run (27.8 to 30.8) is reproduced as unsettled reads, not as the same numbers; its cause is not established.
- compact-fps cannot see the 0.9.1.0 patch (IP 6). The patched 0.9.1.0 whole-run figures are from the checker stream. The two tools disagree on the same stock image (checker 5.7 fps against compact-fps 7.9 at IP 6), so compare only within one tool.

### 42.42 The over-ceiling check on a warm-ramp scene, and a `--flash` part that streams through the checker (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** Two open items of `plan.md` section 1 are answered on the emulator. (1) The 32 Hz copy does not clip, and does not write 0xFFFF, at or above the sensor ceiling (15000): on a scene with samples from 14,880 to 16,370 every delivered sample of the patched 1.3.0.8 and 4.8.2.1 equals its input, exactly as the stock build's does. The superseded one-step op-5 form on the same scene writes 0xFFFF on 679,520 of the 684,480 samples at or above 15000. (2) A `--flash` part now gets its build's 32K sensor when it is booted with `--flash-entry` (FW-V1 `seekemu/cli.py`), and the TypeScript checker streams the patched 1.3.0.0 (2014 chain) and 4.8.2.1 (Key A) parts at 32.26 fps medians, against 32.258 Hz in the Python IP rows. Nothing was run on a camera.

**Tags.** [measured] was read from the run logs and the frames the runs saved; [source] from the code named; [inferred] follows from those.

**1. The scene.** [source] The default 32K scene (the bench 1.3.0.0 recording, `a2_ip3_raw_frames_subset.bin.gz`, 60 frames) has its highest pixel sample at 10,217 (0x27E9); none of its 1,946,880 pixel samples is at or above 15000. Its over-ceiling column in the IP rows is therefore 0.00 %, on stock and patched alike (the default-scene rows below).

The new scene, `WarmRampFrames` in FW-V1 `emu/seekemu/sensor32k.py` (commit `09517806e`), is that recording with one rectangle of every frame's pixels replaced: rows 40 to 119, columns 20 to 169 of the 156 pixel lines, the value 14,880 + 10 per column from column 20. Column 32 is exactly 15,000; column 169 is 16,370, so 0x3FFF is never reached. The header words and every other pixel are the recording's own. `compact_scene()` picks the scene for a 32K boot: the bench recording by default, the warm ramp with `SEEKEMU_32K_SCENE=warm-ramp`. `corpus_baseline.py` (which the IP rows use) and `cli.py` both call it. Each steady frame has 12,000 rectangle halfwords carrying 11,040 samples at or above 15000.

**2. The IP rows on the warm ramp.** `fps_patch_tests.py --only 1.3.0.8@32:ip8 --only 4.8.2.1@32:ip8 --no-long -j 2` with `SEEKEMU_32K_SCENE=warm-ramp`: both rows PASS. The row's columns (its `%ceil` is the share of body halfwords at or above 15000, `%FFFF` the share equal to 0xFFFF):

| build | run | median Hz | level | %ceil | %FFFF |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.3.0.8 | stock | 8.065 | 10210.7 | 35.86 | 0.00 |
| 1.3.0.8 | patched | 32.258 | 10208.4 | 35.86 | 0.00 |
| 4.8.2.1 | stock | 8.065 | 10208.2 | 35.86 | 0.00 |
| 4.8.2.1 | patched | 32.258 | 10213.4 | 35.86 | 0.00 |

35.86 % of the 30,784 body halfwords is 11,040 per frame, the scene's own count at or above 15000: the outputs hold every over-ceiling sample.

**3. Sample by sample.** Four boots (`ceiling_boot.py`, the IP-8 init of the row, 80 frames each; scratch scripts, not committed) saved their raw frames. Each steady frame's rectangle was compared halfword by halfword with the value the scene put there:

| build | run | steady frames | rectangle halfwords | exact | at or above 15000 (expected = output) | clipped to 15000 | 0xFFFF |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.3.0.8 | stock | 58 | 696,000 | 100 % | 640,320 | 0 | 0 |
| 1.3.0.8 | patched (copy, `5313f107`) | 62 | 744,000 | 100 % | 684,480 | 0 | 0 |
| 4.8.2.1 | stock | 50 | 600,000 | 100 % | 552,000 | 0 | 0 |
| 4.8.2.1 | patched (copy) | 55 | 660,000 | 100 % | 607,200 | 0 | 0 |

Column 32 reads 15000, column 33 15010, column 169 16370, in every run. The output's row and column are the sensor's: no shift. [measured]

**4. The control.** The superseded op-5 one-step form was built by hand on the 1.3.0.8 image (steady block `01 0d 0d 00 | 13 25 23 | 00 x9`: op 5 with the publish bit, the acceptance-sum word moved to keep the sum; not a table entry, not committed) and booted the same way. Of the 744,000 rectangle halfwords, 684,480 are at or above 15000: 679,520 read 0xFFFF, and the other 4,960 are column 32, which is exactly 15000 and not above the ceiling; 0 are clipped to 15000. The run's median was 32.258 Hz, so the rate is the same and the picture is not. [measured] So the scene can show the 0xFFFF the op-5 form writes, and the copy form does not write it.

**5. The default scene is unchanged.** `fps_patch_tests.py --only 1.3.0.0@32:ip8`, `--only 1.3.0.8@32:ip8`, `--only 4.8.2.1@32:ip8` (no scene variable): all PASS. 1.3.0.0: 8.065 -> 32.258 Hz, level 6798.1 -> 6797.0; 1.3.0.8: 8.065 -> 32.258 Hz, level 6800.9 -> 6796.9; 4.8.2.1: 8.065 -> 32.258 Hz, level 6796.8 -> 6805.4. The levels are the 42.27 figures. [measured]

**6. The `--flash` part.** [source] Before this change the 32K sensor was attached only for a `--corpus-entry` boot (`cli.py`, `corpus_entry is not None`). A `--flash` part got the SGPIO feed, and the checker received no frames from it (the spec's earlier record, and `e2e/seek-fps-emulator.e2e.ts` before this commit). The FW-V1 change is `--flash-entry ID` (commit `08e1abc6e`): the part boots on that entry's board (straps, VT repair) and gets its 32K sensor, the way `--corpus-entry` does. `packages/core/test/emulator/harness.ts` passes it as `flashEntry`, and `e2e/lib/bench/seek-fps/emulator-link.ts` passes the entry as `flashEntry` for every `flashOverride` boot.

The patched parts (`fps_patch.py`'s `patch_bytes` on the corpus dump, written to a file) were streamed with the checker, `--emulator ENTRY --emulator-flash FILE --fps --mode normal --no-hifps`, `SEEK_EMU_DIR` set to the FW-V1 worktree's `emu`, `SEEK_EMU_PYTHON` to its venv's Python:

| entry | per-second medians (five seconds) | per-second means | overall mean (frames) | Python IP row (default scene) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compact/2014.10.21-14.58.29-1.3.0.0/101310HSNEA2/dump` (1.3.0.0, patched) | 32.26 x5 | 21, 20, 20, 20, 32 | 22.60 (113) | 8.065 -> 32.258 Hz |
| `compact/2020.02.26-11.23.26-4.8.2.1/2229A0YZ7E28/dump` (4.8.2.1, patched) | 32.26 x5 | 19, 18, 18, 32, 32 | 23.80 (119) | 8.065 -> 32.258 Hz |

The medians match the IP rows. The means are lower because the calibration stretch is not patched (`FPS_32HZ.md` section 1). [measured]

### 42.43 The 4.x active-slot word stays 0 because the factory startup never writes it, the 2016 footer is absent from the flash, and modes 4 and 7 are read (emulator only, 2026-10-19)

**Summary.** Three `plan.md` section 1 items (the 4.8.x active-slot word, the 2016 `footerOk`, and modes 4 and 7 with the 0.x masks). Nothing ran on a camera, and no J-Link or switch was used. No harness was changed, so the emulator suite was not re-run and no code changed in this repo.

- **Modes 4 and 7 and the 0.x masks.** Answered in FW-V1 `docs/FRAME_RATE_MODES.md` (commit `7a9b52398`, branch `emu-research`, not merged). Mode 4 on 1.3.0.8 and 4.8.1.7 is a 32.26 Hz stream of live pictures, one per capture. Mode 7 has no capture program and sends a synthetic ramp frame with no sensor picture. The 0.8.0.0 to 0.10.0.0 handlers accept mask `0x1F9` (modes 0, 3 to 8), read from the image bytes.
- **The 4.x active-slot word.** It reads 0 because the factory 4.x startup does not write it. The harness and the emulator both report the value correctly. The bootloader's handoff `R0` does name the right slot.
- **The 2016 `footerOk` false.** It is the flash. The factory 2016 banks have no `CODE` footer at the 4.x offset, and the 2016 verdict does not read `footerOk` at all. The `bootability unknown` comes from the key table, not from the footer.

**Tags.** [measured] is an emulator run or a byte read from a corpus image. [source] is read from the reconstructed C, which is not the build. [inferred] follows from those.

**1. Modes 4 and 7 (summary; detail in FW-V1 `docs/FRAME_RATE_MODES.md`).**

- 1.3.0.8, mode 4 (80 frames, `framerate.run_entry`, IP 4): all 80 frames are type 3, the rate is 32.258 Hz (31.0 ms, device clock), 0 frozen pairs, picture level 6,806 against 6,801 for the mode-8 control. [measured]
- 4.8.1.7, mode 4: the same (32.258 Hz, level 6,806). [measured]
- Mode 7 on both builds: no type-3 frame in 80; the frames are a frame counter plus a ramp (value = pixel index), type word 10. [measured]
- The mode table decode: 1.3.0.8 `frame_mode_table_r32k` at file `0xB45C`, mode 4 is block 23 (one step, op 16, publish), mode 7 is empty. 4.8.1.7 `g_mode_framecfg` at file `0x9B30`, mode 4 is one page at `0x9B80`, mode 7 is empty. [measured, from the image bytes]
- SetIPMode masks of the six 0.x builds with a table entry: `0x1F9` (0, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8), from the `cmp r3,#8; movw r2,#0x1F9` pair in each `cmd_SetIPMode`. [measured]

**2. The 4.x active-slot word (`roots[8]`, GetFirmwareInfo selector 10).**

Where it is read and reported:
- The harness and the core read the word at `packages/core/src/workflows/device-info.ts:556-557` (`tryFwInfo(10, 64, ...)`, offset 8).
- Reported as "booted", not used for the run verdict: `packages/core/src/slots/boot-choice.ts:47-50` (`reportedBootedOf`), and the run verdict comes from `cfg0` (`bootChoiceOf`, lines 136-160).
- Used for the upgrade target only on the 2014 plaintext chain: `device-info.ts:915` (inside the `plainChain` branch at 884-925).
- In FW-V1, the emulator reads the same RAM cell, `G_ACTIVE_SLOT = 0x1000AED0` (`emu/seekemu/flash_rpc.py:53`), and records the bootloader's handoff `R0` (`machine.py:1163-1164`; `flash_rpc.py:643`, `:745`).

What the probe showed (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yrambler2001-things-a-noindex-seek-seek-thermal-firmware-backup/82174575-1341-45d6-a306-7518156cd978/scratchpad/active_slot_probe.py`, a cold boot of the 4.8.2.1 full dump `2229A0YZ7E28`, IP unset, boot word set in the NOR image): [measured]

| boot word | handoff `R0` (slot the bootloader gave) | `0x1000AED0` (active_slot) after the run | `0x1000CF6C` (g_boot_image_flash_base) after the run | `0x1000CDB0` (g_flash_base_offset) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `0x14050000` (slot B) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | `0x14070000` (recovery R) | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The handoff snapshot (taken before the app's own startup) has the same zeros. So the bootloader and the emulator agree on the slot, and the app never writes its cell.

Why the app does not write it (the factory image, not the emulator):
- The 4.8.1.7 startup chunk (vector at `0x100002E1`, so the chunk is `0x100002E0`) is, in the factory bytes, table copy and zero loops followed by a table-driven call. In `0x100002E0..0x10000408` the only compares are loop bounds. No compare against `0x14030000`, `0x14050000` or `0x14070000` appears, and `0x1000CF6C` is not referenced anywhere in the 4.8.1.7 image. [measured, from the disassembly]
- `targets/compact_xr_8hz_4_8_2_1/src/target_startup.c:9-17` says the factory Compact XR body has "no boot-bank arm in it at all and no boot_addr argument - the factory body never reads R0". The arm at `target_startup.c:188-201` is a reconstruction addition, and it is the only writer of `g_fw_info_roots.active_slot` in the source (both the 4.8.1.7 and XR trees). [source]
- So the cell stays 0 from the BSS clear on every boot of a 4.8.x image, whatever the word. The emulator and the harness report that correctly. [inferred from the two points above; the 4.8.2.1 probe covers the XR-target image, and 4.8.1.7 is static only]

Consequences (product code, not changed here):
- The "last start" line that `slots list` and the page show from `reportedBooted` (`boot-choice.ts:47-50`) reads slot A on every 4.x boot, including a boot from B or R. The run verdict is not affected. [inferred from the code and the probe]
- FPS_32HZ.md section 9 says the bootloader writes the word "at every start". That holds for what the 4.x factory app does not do, and it was not checked for the 2014 or 2016 lines here.
- Recommended: on the 4.x line, do not show `reportedBooted` as the booted bank (or show it as "not reported"). The reconstructed `target_startup.c` arm should be marked as not in the factory image.

**3. The 2016 `footerOk` false.**

The analysis (`packages/core/src/workflows/device-info.ts:313-316`) sets `footerOk = footer.tag === FOOTER_TAG && footer.length === header.length`, with the footer at `footerOffsetFor(length)` (`packages/core/src/image/header.ts:102-104`, `((len >> 14) + 1) * 0x4000 - 0x40`). [source]

The flash on the 2016 line has no such footer:
- 1.0.3.0 standard full dump `0C21A1M5KP15` (`emu/data/corpus/compact_pro/2016.07.06-17.04.49-1.0.3.0/0C21A1M5KP15/compact_pro_android_uq-aaa.bin`): bank A is erased; bank B and R hold a 51,848-byte image (`0xCA88`). The footer position `0xFFC0` in each bank is `FF` x 16. No byte after `0xCA88` in bank B is other than `FF`, and the string `CODE` does not occur in bank B. [measured]
- The 2014 control, 1.3.0.0 full dump `101310HSNEA2`: bank R (`len 0xBA98`) has `FF` at its footer position `0xBFC0`. So the factory 2014 banks also carry no footer. The footer that FW-V1's J-Link runner writes ("padded to 0xBFC0, then CODE") is the writer's convention, not what the factory leaves. [measured]
- The 2016 bootloader does not read a footer. Its boot path decrypts the header, copies the sections and jumps (`targets/compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0_bootloader/src/startup.c:150-200`). [source]
- The 2016 profile uses `LEGACY_BOOT` (`packages/core/src/profiles/compact-2016.ts:300`), whose `checksFooter` is false (`legacy-auth.ts:586-587`, and the `BootPolicy` note in `types.ts:158-166`). So `footerPasses` is true (`device-info.ts:775`), and the verdict ternary at `device-info.ts:776-786` does not read `footerOk`.

So `footerOk false` is the analysis reading the flash correctly. It is not an emulator artifact. The 42.36 banks written by the harness also report `footerOk` false, which matches a 2016 write that adds no footer. [inferred from 42.36's report]

The `bootability unknown` on the 2016 line comes from another branch: `device-info.ts:783` (`slot.present && slot.accepts && footerPasses && keyTable === null`). `keyTable` is null because no candidate key table matches the 2016 keystream state (`device-info.ts:711-722`), and the 2016 line's acceptance is the sum 0 with K=0 (`compact-2016.ts`). [source; the key-table miss is inferred from the null result]

Recommended, product decision, not changed here:
- Report `footerOk` as not applicable when `profile.boot.checksFooter` is false, instead of `false`.
- For the 2016 line, the verdict needs a key table or a boot-word replay. The page then says "bootable" for the bank the bootloader runs, not "unknown". The 4.x line already replays the boot word (`modern-4x.ts`, `MODERN_BOOT`).

**4. Counts.** Emulator runs: 6 IP-mode boots (1.3.0.8 and 4.8.1.7, IP 8, 4, 7), 3 frame dumps (1.3.0.8 mode 4 and 7, 4.8.1.7 mode 7), 2 cold boots of the 4.8.2.1 dump (words 1 and 2). Static reads: 6 0.x `cmd_SetIPMode` handlers, the 4.8.1.7 mode table and page, the 1.3.0.8 mode table and blocks, and 3 full dumps (the 2016 1.0.3.0 and the 2014 1.3.0.0 controls, and the 4.8.2.1). Test suites run: none. Harness changes: none.

**5. Not measured or open.**
- No camera: the mode-4 rate on a Compact is not measured; the 32.26 Hz is the emulator's device clock.
- The active-slot cause is shown on the 4.8.2.1 image by the probe and on 4.8.1.7 by the chunk disassembly only. The 4.8.1.9 image has the `0x1000AEC8` literal once (not checked). Word 0 was not probed (it reads 0 by construction).
- Mode 4 over a longer stream: the calibration stretch was not checked beyond 2.5 s.
- The 2014 chain's own bootloader (`compact_8hz_1_3_0_0_bootloader/src/startup.c:154`) passes no slot argument to the entry. Whether the 2014 app writes the cell was not checked.
- The `footerOk` recommendation and the key-table gap are for the owner's decision.

### 42.44 The slots table stays after a write (read again under the write's own profile, with no identify probe); the Info tab's identity read and the CLI `info` read are recorded as deliberate, nothing changed (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** Two plan items. (1) After a committed write the slots page dropped its read, so the bank table stayed empty until "Read slots" was pressed. The read is still dropped at the commit point, and the banks are read again after the read-back, under the write's own profile and build. Changed in `packages/web/src/hooks/useSlotsPanel.ts` (commit `ffaa310`), with tests in `useSlotsPanel.test.tsx` and `SlotsView.test.tsx`. (2) The CLI `info` sends SetFirmwareInfoFeatures (0x55) and SetRAMDataFeatures (0x5a) and reads the slots; the web Info sends neither. The difference is deliberate: 42.17 made the Info tab an identity read. Nothing was changed for item 2; the options are below. Nothing ran on a camera.

**Tags.** [measured] is a test run, or a read of the code on this branch that was checked by grep. [inferred] is what follows from the code and was not run.

**1. The bank table after a write.**

- **Cause [measured].** `write` in `useSlotsPanel.ts` called `forgetReport()` in its `finally` once the write was committing. With no report, `SlotsView` unmounts the table and shows "Press Read slots". Core already reads the bank back: `flashSlot` returns the read-back and its verdict (`after`, `verified`, `packages/core/src/slots/write.ts`). The page threw that read-back away with the report.
- **Change.** The report is dropped at the commit point, before `backend.flash` (`useSlotsPanel.ts:878-879`), so nothing after the commit can use the old read. When the flash returns, whatever its verdict (`verified` true, false or null), `readAfterWrite` reads the banks again with `backend.inspect` on the same client, under the report's own profile and version (`useSlotsPanel.ts:495`, called at `:900`). Read slots is unchanged.
- **No identify probe after the commit.** The identify step runs `probeSelectorChannel` (`packages/core/src/workflows/capability.ts`), which sends a plain and then an authenticated BeginFirmwareUpgrade on a protected subcommand. [measured in code] Nothing after a commit should arm more than the banks' own read does, so the re-read reuses the profile the write was sent under. [inferred]
- **Failures stay honest.** A failed or cancelled re-read is logged as a warning, the write's outcome stays, and the report stays null, so no bank is shown as read. A write the page refuses before the commit (no acknowledgement, a stale report) keeps the read it was made from. A refusal core makes inside `flashSlot`, before any byte is sent, is still after the commit point and drops the read, as before.
- **Why a re-read and not a patch of one row.** The read-back is the raw bytes of one bank. The table's rows are core's analysis of the whole camera (`inspectSlots`, which calls `readDeviceInfo`), and core has no one-bank analysis from bytes. [inferred from `slots/inspect.ts` and `slots/write.ts`]
- **What the table shows before the replug.** The version and the active bank settle only after a power cycle. The table after a write shows the camera's answers as they stand before the replug. The outcome panel already says so, and the log line for the re-read says so.

Tests, all targeted, no camera:

- `packages/web/src/hooks/useSlotsPanel.test.tsx`: 43 of 43 (39 before, 4 new). The test "writes it only after the confirmation" now asserts the table is read again; it used to assert the table was null. New: the table shows the re-read report and not the one from before, with the identify probe run once; a read-back that does not match keeps the table and says so; a failed re-read keeps the outcome and shows no bank as read; a write refused before the commit keeps its read.
- `packages/web/src/views/SlotsView.test.tsx`: 44 of 44 (3 new). The table stays on screen after a write, with the outcome above it; a read-back that does not match keeps the table and says it does NOT match; no read after a write shows no table, no "reads back as written", and the Read slots prompt.
- `packages/web/src/views/SlotsView.verdicts.test.tsx`: 6 of 6, unchanged.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/web/tsconfig.app.json`: exit 0. eslint and prettier on the three files: clean.

**Not verified.** On a camera, a read straight after a commit with no reset is not known to be answered. If it is not, the page logs it and the table stays empty, as it did before this change. The re-read is not proven on hardware.

**2. CLI `info` and the web Info: the two read paths.**

- **Web Info** (`packages/web/src/hooks/useInfoPanel.ts`, core `readRunningFirmware`). Two GetFirmwareInfo reads, with the operation-mode and error-code reads. Nothing is armed, no slot is read, and it sends neither 0x55 nor 0x5a. `useInfoPanel.test.tsx`, "sends only the identity read", pins the wire to those three requests. [measured]
- **CLI `info`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/info.ts`, `analyseCamera`). The identify probe (`identifyCamera`, which arms, unless `--profile` or `--no-probe` is given), then core's `readDeviceInfo`. That sends SetFirmwareInfoFeatures (0x55) for selectors 1, 20, 17 and 10 (`packages/core/src/workflows/device-info.ts:540-556`), SetRamDataFeatures (0x5a) for the device-id block (`client.ts:405`, `device-info.ts:559`), and arms the boot config, the bootloader block and the slots through `armWindow`. [measured]
- **Web Slots page.** `CORE_SLOTS_BACKEND` (`useSlotsPanel.ts`): `identify` is the same `identifyCamera` probe, then `inspectSlots`, which calls `readDeviceInfo`. So the CLI `info` and the web Slots page already share one read sequence through core. The web Info is the only path that does not. [measured]
- **Dumps do not reach it.** `readDeviceInfo` is called only by `inspectSlots` (the slots page, and the CLI `slots`) and by the CLI `info`. `readFwInfo`, `tryFwInfo` and `readSerial` are called only from `device-info.ts`. No dump, sweep or preserve path calls either, so the `FLASH_OPS` rule (nothing in it runs during a dump) holds. [measured by grep of `packages/core/src` and `packages/cli/src`]
- **What the two setters do.** 0x55 latches a selector in the camera's RAM (`g_fw_info_selector`); the next GetFirmwareInfo returns that record and clears the latch. It writes nothing in flash (TESTING.md lines 1838-1870 and 6732-6734). The latch outlives the host session, so a setter that is never read leaves the next unarmed read returning another record. That is why `readRunningFirmware` reads twice and why 0x55 is not sent before identity. 0x5a arms the RAM device-id block for the next ordinary read (`client.ts:403-412`). Neither is a flash write. [measured in the code and TESTING.md; the emulator notes say the same]
- **History.** 42.16 (2026-10-18): the CLI `info` "reads the camera as before". 42.17 (commit `d3a82dc`): the web Info became "reads the firmware version (read-only)" with "Nothing else", and the device info moved to the Slots page, "the same read as its bank table". Its hook header says "No selector is armed, no slot is read and nothing is written." 42.18: recorded as "Recorded, not changed. ... Both are the read paths as they were built."

Options for the owner. Nothing was changed.

- **A. Keep both (recommended).** The Info tab stays an identity read, and the full read stays on `info` and the Slots page. Evidence: the 42.17 decision, the Info text, and the pinned Info wire test. The bench calls `seek-fw info --json` (42.16), so the CLI's output would change under option C. The `FLASH_OPS` rule is intact.
- **B. Give the web Info the full read.** The Info tab would send 0x55 and 0x5a, arm the boot config and the slots, and send the probe's arms. That breaks its stated contract ("Nothing else"), fails "sends only the identity read", and repeats the Slots page's read on the landing tab. Only if the owner wants the landing tab to show the slots.
- **C. Make the CLI `info` identity-only.** That removes the slot table, the boot data and the serial from `info` and from `info --json`, which the bench reads. Not recommended.

**Not verified.** Nothing ran on a camera. No CLI test pins the `info` wire: the only CLI test that names 0x55 is `emulator-host-giveup.test.ts`, which is a bench-only emulator test. So the CLI path's wire is checked by reading the code, not by a test.

**3. Noted, not changed.**

- The frame-rate patch (`patchFps`) drops its report after a patch the same way (`if (used) forgetReport()`). The same fix would apply. It is not in the plan item and is left as it is.
- `packages/core/src/protocol/ops.ts:44` says 0x55 and 0x5a are "used by the flash path only". The info read uses them too, through `readDeviceInfo`. The `FLASH_OPS` header's dump rule is correct; the comment at `:44` is narrower than the code.

### 42.45 The retained memory of the slots bench was the Vite dev server each window started, not Electron: one shared server per run takes the window path from +465 MB to +28 MB over 24 windows (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** The 42.21 finding (about 200 MB per subject, 22 to 30 MB per Electron window, not located) is located, and it is not in Electron. Each bench window (`openBenchPage` through `openTarget('camera')` on the dev source) started its own Vite dev server and closed it with the window. After `close()`, a Vite 8.3.0 dev server's module graph stays reachable, and the transformed code of the page's modules stays in the test worker's heap. The fix is one dev server per process: the windows of a run share it, and the owner closes it when the run ends. On the window path the worker's retained heap went from +465 MB (3 subjects of 8 windows) and +500 MB (2 subjects of 13 windows) to +28 MB once per run. The fake-mode bench opens no windows, so the fix does not change it. The 42.21 figure of about 1 MB per start and close was for a start and close of the same config with no page load (its wording); with the page's modules loaded it is 18 to 31 MB per start and close.

**Tags.** [measured] is read from the probe logs, the heap snapshots and the bench logs. [inferred] is what follows from them.

**1. What was ruled out, and the reproduction.**

- The fake-mode bench does not reproduce the growth: `createFakeRig` opens no Electron window (`spec-fakes.ts`, "no hardware, no Electron"), and the per-window heap lines are written only by `openBenchPage`. Its per-subject heap stayed at 39 MB across both fake subjects. [measured]
- Electron alone. A window on the static `docs/` bundle, with no Vite server, through `ElectronApp.launch` (the same launcher, no camera, no `connect`): the worker's heap went 27 to 29 MB over three windows (deltas +1, +1, 0). The Electron processes are separate processes and are not in the worker's heap. [measured]
- The Vite dev server with no Electron. A server started, the page and its modules fetched, and the server closed: +31 and +24 MB per cycle in one run; +30, +18 and +24 MB in a second run. [measured]
- The bench's own window path (an Electron window on a per-window dev server, no camera): +31, +23 and +22 MB per window. [measured]
- So the growth belongs to the dev server. The 42.21 note named the server as ruled out, but it was measured with no page load.

**2. The evidence: heap snapshots.** Two heap snapshots of the dev-only run, after cycle 1 and cycle 3 (`v8.writeHeapSnapshot`, 31 MB and 41 MB on disk), diffed by V8 object id (`analyze-snap.mjs`). 117,601 objects are new, 39.5 MB of self size. [measured]

- The largest new groups are the transformed code of the page's modules (`string`, for example the `import { t as __commonJSMin } …` module wrappers at 3.6 MB and 5.3 MB, and the lucide and React license headers), then arrays, objects and closures. No `Uint8Array` or bank image is among the top groups, so the bench's own images are not the growth. [measured]
- The retaining path of the largest new strings: `(Global handles)` → closure `onWarn` (the rolldown bundler options of Vite's `DevEnvironment`) → its context → the `getEnv` closure → `envs` → `DevEnvironment` → `moduleGraph` → `EnvironmentModuleNode` → `transformResult.code`. The `onWarn` and `onLog` callbacks are passed into rolldown's native binding (`@rolldown/binding-darwin-arm64`). The snapshot shows a global handle still holding the `onWarn` closure after the server closed. Which part of the binding holds it is [inferred]; the binding source was not read. [measured path, inferred owner]
- One other path in the snapshot ran from the probe's own last-server variable (`(Stack roots)` → the probe's `close` closure). That is the probe holding its last server, not the leak. [measured]

**3. The numbers, the same probe in both modes.** A probe (`zz-window-probe.e2e.ts`, scratch only, not committed) launches `ElectronApp` on `#/`, lets the page settle for 1.5 s, closes the window, and measures the worker heap after two collections. `per-window` starts a dev server per window (the old path); `shared` uses one `sharedDevServer()` for the run. [measured]

| Run                            | Subjects x windows | Worker heap growth per subject | Total   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------- |
| per-window dev server (before) | 3 x 8              | +168, +148, +149 MB            | +465 MB |
| shared dev server (after)      | 3 x 8              | +28, +1, 0 MB                  | +28 MB  |
| per-window dev server (before) | 2 x 13             | +260, +241 MB                  | +500 MB |
| shared dev server (after)      | 2 x 13             | +29, +0 MB                     | +28 MB  |

The 13 windows per subject are the count in the bench flow: the fake run opens 13 windows for each of its two subjects (a temporary counter in `openPage`, reverted). These Makefiles say `TARGET_IMAGE ?= $(BUILD)/image.bin` with `BUILD ?= build`, so `build_flash.mjs` looks for the literal `$(BUILD)/image.bin`. [measured] `make -n -C targets/compact_8hz_1_3_0_0 target-image` prints `--out build/image.bin`. With a stub `make` that writes where the Makefile says, the real `build_flash.mjs` stops before any J-Link call: `build finished but .../$(BUILD)/image.bin is missing`. That holds for 18 of the 19 before and after this change, and for the five targets of f5995f8d9 (1.3.0.0, 1.3.0.8, 0.5.1.3, 0.9.0.2, 1.0.0.0). [measured] Only `compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0` reaches `flash-bank` under a real make, and it now writes 0x14060000 with boot word 1. So today the wrong-bank write is reachable on that one target only. f5995f8d9's offline check and 42.40's reached `flash-bank`, so their stub must have written the literal `$(BUILD)` path, which a real make does not ([inferred] from their reported calls). Fixing the path is a choice for the owner (for example, pass `BUILD` into the expansion with its default `build`), and it was not made here, since the brief asked for the table only.

### 42.47 The frame-rate patch keeps the bank table after a patch (read again after the read-back); the `ops.ts:44` comment names the device-info read (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** Two plan items. (1) The frame-rate patch (`patchFps`) dropped the bank table after a patch, as the write did before 42.44. It now follows the same approach: the report is dropped at the commit point, right before the core's patch is called, and after the read-back the banks are read again with `readAfterWrite`, under the report's own profile and version, with no identify probe. This closes the note at 42.44 item 3. Changed in `packages/web/src/hooks/useSlotsPanel.ts`, with tests in `useSlotsPanel.test.tsx` and `SlotsView.test.tsx`. (2) `packages/core/src/protocol/ops.ts:44` said 0x55 and 0x5a are "used by the flash path only". The comment now names the device-info read as the other user, and says no dump sends them. The code is unchanged. The worktree was reset to `refactor/all-firmware-profiles` at `1e16c29`; its old HEAD `cf5420b` is an ancestor of it, so no commit was dropped. Nothing ran on a camera.

**Tags.** [measured] is a test run, or a read of the code checked by grep. [inferred] is what follows from the code and was not run.

**1. The frame-rate patch keeps the bank table.**

- **Cause [measured].** `patchFps` set `used` once the transport was open, and its `finally` called `forgetReport()` when `used` was set. So every patch that reached the core dropped its read. A patch the page refused before that point (no report, the risk tick missing) kept it.
- **Change.** The commit point is the same as in `write`: `committing = true` and `forgetReport()` sit right before the core's patch call (`useSlotsPanel.ts:1005-1006`), and the `finally` no longer forgets the report. After the read-back, `readAfterWrite(current, client, signal, 'patch')` reads the banks again (`:1022`), under the report's own profile and build. `readAfterWrite` (`:495`) takes the name of the commit, so its log lines say "after the patch" or "after the write"; the write's lines are otherwise unchanged. The write's commit point and re-read are at `:883-884` and `:905`.
- **Failures stay honest.** A failed or cancelled re-read is logged as a warning. The patch result stays, and the report stays null, so no bank is shown as read. The cancel message after a commit still says the bank may be partly written.
- **Core refusals after the commit.** A refusal inside `patchBankFps` after the commit point (the pre-patch dump not saved) drops the read, as a refusal inside `flashSlot` does under 42.44. [inferred from the code; the existing test "a dump that was not saved refuses the patch" does not assert the table.]
- **A patched bank is not offered again.** The re-read bank is planned from its own image by `fpsPlanOfBank`, then `planFpsPatch`. An image that matches a patched entry comes back `status: 'patched'`, "already patched ... so no patch is offered" (`packages/core/src/preservation/fps-patch.ts:474`). [measured in code; not run on a patched image.]

Tests, all targeted, no camera:

- `packages/web/src/hooks/useSlotsPanel.test.tsx`: 48 of 48 (43 before, 5 new, from line 1163). New: the table shows the banks read again after a patch, not the read from before, with the identify probe run once; a read-back that does not match keeps the table and says so; a failed re-read keeps the patch result and shows no bank as read; a cancelled re-read is logged and keeps the patch result; a patch the page refuses before anything is sent (the risk tick missing) keeps the read it was made from.
- `packages/web/src/views/SlotsView.test.tsx`: 47 of 47 (44 before, 3 new, from line 1055). New: the table stays on screen after a patch, with the outcome above it; a read-back that does not match keeps the table and says it does NOT differ only as planned; no read after a patch shows no table, keeps the outcome, and asks for Read slots.
- `packages/web/src/views/SlotsView.verdicts.test.tsx`: 6 of 6, unchanged.
- Mutation check [measured]: with the HEAD hook (the patch drops its report) in place, the four re-read tests fail. The refused-before-commit test passes on both versions, as it should. The hook was restored and checked byte for byte afterwards.

**2. The `ops.ts:44` comment.**

- **Where 0x55 and 0x5a are sent [measured].** `readFwInfo` sends SetFirmwareInfoFeatures (0x55) (`packages/core/src/protocol/client.ts:369`), and `readSerial` sends SetRamDataFeatures (0x5a) (`client.ts:411`). `readDeviceInfo` calls both: `tryFwInfo` for selectors 1, 20, 17 and 10, and `readSerial` (`packages/core/src/workflows/device-info.ts:540-559`). `readDeviceInfo` is reached from `inspectSlots` (`packages/core/src/slots/inspect.ts:77` and `:92`), which is the slots page's bank read and the CLI `slots` (`packages/cli/src/commands/slots.ts:121`), and from the CLI `info` (`packages/cli/src/commands/info.ts:344` and `:359`).
- **Where they are not sent [measured].** The dump paths (the CLI `dump`, the slot dump in `packages/core/src/slots/dump.ts`, and the web dump page) read the firmware through `readRunningFirmware` (`packages/core/src/workflows/capability.ts:340`), which reads GetFirmwareInfo unarmed and sends neither opcode (`capability.ts:289`). The web Info uses it too. No dump path reaches `readDeviceInfo`, so the `FLASH_OPS` rule (nothing in it runs during a dump) holds, as 42.44 found.
- **The comment now says** the group is used by the flash path, that 0x55 and 0x5a are also used by the device-info read (the CLI info and slots, and the slots page), and that no dump sends them.
- No test pins the comment text. A grep found it only in `ops.ts` and the built `dist` copy.
- **Left alone.** The `FLASH_OPS` header still describes the set as "the info reads that only the flash path needs". The CLI `info` needs the same reads, so that sentence is as narrow as the old comment was. It is outside `:44`, which the brief named, so it is not changed. For the owner to decide.

**Checks [measured].**

### 42.48 The 42.43 follow-ups: the active-slot word is a booted bank only on the 2014 chain, footerOk is not applicable where no footer is checked, the fps bench shares one dev server, and the stale texts are corrected (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** Four plan items from 42.43 and 42.45, and the 4.x upgrade-target override that 42.43 did not reach. Nothing ran on a camera, and the J-Link and the USB switch were not used. (1) The active-slot word is reported as the booted bank only on the 2014 plaintext chain. On 4.x and 2016 `bootChoiceOf` reports none. No 4.x text printed the word before this change, so no CLI or page text changed; the value did. (2) `info --json` gives `footerOk` as null where the profile's bootloader reads no footer. Its text already said "n/a". (3) `e2e/fps-bench.e2e.ts` shares one dev server per run and closes it. (4) The stale texts in FPS_32HZ.md (sections 9 and 10) and in FW-V1's 1.3.0.8 comments are corrected. No 2016 key table was built; item 3 lists what one would need. One finding is left for the owner: the word also overrides the 4.x upgrade target (item 1).

**Tags.** [measured] is a test run or a byte read from a corpus image. [source] is read from code or source comments. [inferred] follows from them.

**1. The active-slot word (roots[8], the cell at 0x1000AED0).**

- **What the word is [source].** It is the app's RAM word. The bootloader does not write the cell. It records the slot it enters in the warm-boot handoff (`compact_8hz_1_3_0_0_bootloader/src/startup.c:142-150`, `compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0_bootloader/src/startup.c:188-194`: `handoff->slot`, 0 A, 1 B, 2 R). So 42.43's "the bootloader writes it" named the handoff, not the cell. The 1.3.0.0 tree has no writer. The 4.x factory app does not write it (42.43). Whether the 2014 and 2016 factory images write it was not checked: those writers are reconstructions, and neither factory image was disassembled here.

After: the same text on the 2014 chain; nothing on 4.x or 2016.

- **Risks.**

A coincidental match would name a wrong key, and a bank the bootloader skips could read as bootable, or the reverse. Require the same table to confirm on two banks, on both 1.0.3.0 and 1.0.3.2 units.
  - The 9 Hz builds share one key pair (`capability-notes.ts`, the 2016 note). A table from one unit holds for the build family, but the per-device key slot is per unit, so keep it read from each camera's own block.
  - Do not embed the table in the profile. A later build would inherit it without a check.

### 42.49 The FW-V1 build path, the bootloader targets and the 1.3.0.8 footer: make's BUILD is read in 24 targets, the bootloaders refuse before make, and the 1.3.0.8 footer goes after its image (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** The three FW-V1 `plan.md` items, on branch `plan-hygiene` in the FW-V1 worktree `/private/tmp/claude-501/fwv1-hygiene`, three commits on top of 42.46's `1b4faceeb`: `b99426f8b` (the image path), `289548951` (the bootloader targets) and `3c3e688ea` (the 1.3.0.8 footer). Nothing was merged to FW-V1 main or pushed, and FW-V1's main checkout was not touched. The seek worktree was reset to `refactor/all-firmware-profiles` at `2744ad1`, as the brief asked; its old HEAD `cf5420b` is an ancestor of it. No camera, J-Link or USB switch was used. Every check ran in a sandbox holding a copy of one target's `tools/`, `Makefile` and `base/`, with a stub `make` that asks the real GNU make (`gmake`) where `TARGET_IMAGE` points and copies a stand-in image there, a logging `JLinkExe` that talks to nothing (`JLINKEXE` pointed at it), and the real `build_flash.mjs`, `package_image.py` and `jlink-runner.js`.

**Tags.** [measured] is a command run in this session. [inferred] is read from the code and not run.

**1. The image path (FW-V1 `b99426f8b`).**
- Cause [measured]. `build_flash.mjs` expanded `TARGET_IMAGE` with `BASE_DIR`, `FIRMWARE_TARGET` and `TARGET_BUILD` only. Twenty-three of the 24 Makefiles say `TARGET_IMAGE ?= $(BUILD)/image.bin` with `BUILD ?= build`, so the script looked for the literal `$(BUILD)/image.bin`. Before the fix, 21 of the 24 stopped with `build finished but .../$(BUILD)/image.bin is missing`; the two bootloader targets without a base folder have no stand-in in the sandbox and were not reached.
- The real make's image path, from `gmake -n target-image` in each tree (nothing executed) [measured]: `build/image.bin` for 23. `compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0` recurses with `BUILD=build/targets/compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0` and writes `--output build/targets/compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0/image.bin`, the path its `TARGET_IMAGE` already expands to.
- Fix: `vars.BUILD = makeVar(makefile, "BUILD", "build")` in the 24 copies. The one target that takes its image from `TARGET_BUILD` is unchanged.
- A side fact [measured]. A PATH miss in the sandbox ran the real GNU make on the 1.3.0.0 target, which built `build/image.bin` (47768 B). That image is byte-identical to the factory oracle. So the bytes are right; only the lookup was wrong.

**2. The bootloader targets (FW-V1 `289548951`).**
- What the three name [measured]. `compact_8hz_1_3_0_0_bootloader` names `base/compact_8hz_1_3_0_0_bootloader`, which is not in its tree. `compact_pro_ff_18hz_1_0_3_0_bootloader` names `base/compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0`, which its PRO FF base does not hold. `compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0_bootloader` has its base folder, but no `bootloader_to_be_reconstructed_full_flash.bin`. Each `base` is a symlink to another target's `base`.
- What they should point to [measured]. Each bootloader image is byte-identical (sha256) to the first 64 KB of the 4 MB `firmware_to_be_reconstructed_full_flash.bin` in the same folder: `base/compact_8hz_1_3_0_0`, `base/compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0` (the file there is named `.BIN`) and `base/compact_pro_ff_18hz_1_0_3_0`. So the factory-flash file is that camera's own 4 MB dump, and the PRO FF bootloader's own folder is the PRO FF one, not the 9 Hz one its Makefile names.
- Why the targets are refused rather than pointed there [measured]. A bootloader image has no app header: words 0x200 and 0x204 are both 0. `package_image.py` stamps it and builds a 0x14000-byte payload, which exceeds the 64K upgrade window (`ValueError: bank payload 0x14000 exceeds the 64K upgrade window`). So it is not a bank image.
- Fix: `preflight()` in the 24 copies runs before make. It refuses, naming the missing BASE_DIR or the missing factory-flash file, with "nothing was built". The three bootloader targets are refused. So are the 18 application targets whose base folder holds no `firmware_to_be_reconstructed_full_flash.bin`; before, they built and then stopped at `packageBank`. No reference file was added to any tree.
- Real trees, no stand-ins [measured]: `compact_8hz_1_3_0_0`, `compact_pro_9hz_1_0_3_0` and `compact_pro_ff_18hz_1_0_3_0` reach flash-bank. The other 21 refuse before make, each naming the file or folder.

**3. The 1.3.0.8 footer (FW-V1 `3c3e688ea`).**
- Which value is right. `header.length` 0xBFE8 is right [measured]: it is the file size (49128 B), and the 2014 bootloader's `image_sum_ok` (bootloader 0x14000634, `src/crypto.c`) sums exactly that many bytes. The footer offset 0xBFC0 is wrong for this image: `((0xBFE8>>14)+1)*0x4000 - 0x40` lies inside the image, on its last 40 bytes. The 2014 bootloader reads no footer, and the factory 2014 and 2016 banks carry none: the 1.3.0.0 dump's slot A and recovery have no `CODE` at 0xBFC0, and the PRO 1.0.3.0 and PRO FF 1.0.3.0 dumps have none at 0xFFC0 [measured]. The footer is the 4.x `boot_main` convention, which the docs describe [inferred from the docs and `FLASHING_TROUBLESHOOTING.md`].
- Overwrite? [measured] No. `package_image.py` and `seek_fw_tool.mjs` both raise `image (0xbfe8) overruns footer slot (0xbfc0)` before writing anything. But the runner's footer guard and `build_flash`'s `validateBank` carry the same formula, so none of the four could build a 1.3.0.8 bank.
- Fix: the footer is the first page end at or after `length + 0x40`: `((((length + 0x3F) >> 14) + 1) * 0x4000) - 0x40`. It equals `boot_main`'s formula except where that value falls inside the image. For 0xBFE8 it is 0xFFC0, a 0x10000 B payload inside the 64K window. Changed in the 1.3.0.8 copies of `package_image.py`, `seek_fw_tool.mjs`, `build_flash.mjs` and `jlink/jlink-runner.js` (two lines).
- The other images [measured]. The same formula was checked over 69 images (the tree's base folders and the corpus manifest). Only the 1.3.0.8 image (0xBFE8, two entries) changes, and no image's new footer is inside the image or past 64K. The copies in the other targets, `codegen/` and `emu/` give the same offsets for every image in the tree, so they are not changed.
- Test [measured]. `package_image.py` loaded from this target: `footer_offset(0xBFE8) = 0xFFC0`; equal to the old value wherever the old footer was after the image. The 1.3.0.8 image packages to 0x10000 B, with the packaged image in front, 0xFF between, and `CODE` and length 0xBFE8 at 0xFFC0.

**4. The sandbox runs, all 24 (stub `make`, logging `JLinkExe`).** The "before" column is HEAD's `build_flash.mjs` with a stand-in factory file where the base folder lacks one. "Stand-in" means a copy of the 1.3.0.0 dump placed as the missing factory file, in the sandbox only. Boot word and bank are read from the `loadbin` calls.

**5. Found, not changed.**
- **The 2014 bank format.** [measured] The 1.3.0.0 dump's slot A (0x14050000) is the decrypted image byte for byte, and its word sum over `header.length` is 0. ### 42.50 The 4.x upgrade target is the camera's own upgrade destination on every boot measured, so the word override stays; the 2016 rekey warning does not fire, by design, and the code and tests say why (2026-10-19)

**Summary.** Two items from `plan.md` section 1: the 4.x upgrade target, and the 2016 rekey warning. Emulator only: no camera, J-Link or USB switch was used. (1) The code's upgrade target matches the camera's own upgrade destination on all six boots measured (the Compact 4.8.2.1 and the Compact PRO 4.9.1.15 dumps, boot words 0, 1 and 2). The fix the plan describes, gating the active-slot word out of `device-info.ts:944` the way 42.48 gated `bootChoiceOf`, makes the 4.8.2.1 boots with words 1 and 2 name slot A, where the camera writes slot B. So `device-info.ts` is unchanged, and a new emulator test pins the picks. (2) The rekey warning cannot fire on 2016 and should not: the 2016 line never reaches either site, and on 2016 bootability is "unknown", not "not bootable". Both sites now say so in a comment, and three tests pin the 4.x rule and the 2016 gate. The change is comments and tests only.

**Tags.** [measured] is an emulator run, or a read-only probe of the emulator. [source] is read from code. [inferred] follows from those.

**1. The 4.x upgrade target (`device-info.ts:944`, `confirmUpgradeTarget`).**

Before, as the test shows it. Each row boots the full dump with the boot-config word at `0x14010000` set, and reads the device info the way the page does. The code's pick is `boot.target`. [measured]

| dump | cfg[0] | active-slot word | replay boots | window confirms | code picks | camera's own destination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compact 4.8.2.1 | 0 | 0 | A | neither (A and B are identical) | B | B |
| Compact 4.8.2.1 | 1 | 0 | B | neither | B | B |
| Compact 4.8.2.1 | 2 | 0 | R | neither | B | B |
| Compact PRO 4.9.1.15 | 0 | 0 | A | B | B | B |
| Compact PRO 4.9.1.15 | 1 | 0 | A (B is not bootable in this dump) | B | B | B |
| Compact PRO 4.9.1.15 | 2 | 2 | R | A | A | A |

On 4.8.2.1 with words 1 and 2 the replay names A ("booted Slot B, so an upgrade would write Slot A"; "booted Recovery, so an upgrade would write Slot A"). The active-slot word is 0, so the override says "Slot B instead — trusting the camera". The window matches both A and B, so it cannot overrule, and B stands.

The camera's own answer. `upgrade_target_probe.py` (in the session scratchpad, `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yrambler2001-things-a-noindex-seek-seek-thermal-firmware-backup/82174575-1341-45d6-a306-7518156cd978/scratchpad/`) cold-boots the same dump with the word set, arms selector 0 with the two-byte payload the code sends, and reads `g_fw_op_desc.dest`. It is read-only: a copy-on-write NOR, and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` so nothing under FW-V1 is written. In the emulator the upgrade commit (81) programs the slot at `dest`, and `upgrade_phase` reads the slot back there (`seekemu/flash_rpc.py`). So `dest` is the upgrade target. [measured] Results: 4.8.2.1, B for words 0, 1 and 2. 4.9.1.15 PRO, B, B and A. Forcing the active-slot cell `0x1000AED0` to 1 or 2 before the arm left the 4.8.2.1 destination at B, and so did forcing `0x10000208` to 2. So the RAM word that mode 0 reads on 4.8.2.1 was not found; the outcome was measured, the input was not.

The gate the plan describes. `if (activeSlotWord !== null && plainChain)`, the 42.48 gate applied at line 944, fails the 4.8.2.1 rows for words 1 and 2: it names A, and the camera writes B. The other four rows still pass. It was run and reverted; `device-info.ts` has no diff. [measured]

Why the code is right here. [inferred]
- Where the window tells A from B, it is the camera's answer: it reads the block the selector arms (`confirmUpgradeTarget`), and the code trusts it over the replay. The PRO rows show it.
- Where the window cannot tell them apart, as on the identical banks of the 4.8.2.1 dump, the active-slot word decides. The rule the code states for that, active slot 0 gives B and anything else gives A, matches the camera on all six boots.
- The replay's rule (booted A gives B, otherwise A) is the part that disagrees with the camera, on 4.8.2.1 with words 1 and 2. TESTING.md 27.2 defines the upgrade target as mode 0 itself, which is the camera's answer, so the replay is the prediction to drop.

Corrections. [measured] 42.43 and 42.48 say the active-slot word is always 0 on 4.x. It is 0 on 4.8.2.1 under every word. On the Compact PRO 4.9.1.15 it read 2 when the replay booted R, and 0 when it booted A. Word 1 boots A in this dump because the replay finds B not bootable. TESTING.md 8937 records words 1 and 2 reading 1 and 2 on the 4.9.x Compact PRO. So "always 0 on 4.x" holds for 4.8.x only.

For the owner. [measured on the emulator, not a camera] On the Compact 4.8.2.1 with the word at 1 or 2, the camera's own upgrade writes slot B, the bank it booted from. The page shows "Booted from B" and "Upgrade target B" together. Whether the page should say so is the owner's call. The replay log line "so an upgrade would write Slot A" is wrong for this build; it is followed by the override, and it is left as it is.

Not changed: `device-info.ts`, and the 2014 chain (its gate and its word reading are as 42.48 left them).

**2. The 2016 rekey warning (`write.ts:565`, `flash.ts:437`).**

What it says. [source] `rekeyRisk` warns that the target "already holds an image the bootloader cannot take", so the write "lands in the same state". The condition is present, accepts, `footerOk` and not `bootable`.

Where it can be reached. [source]
- `write.ts:565` is the `key-a-ciphertext` branch. `stagingFor` gives that staging to the modern family only. The 2016 line stages `slot-keystream-ciphertext`, and that branch sets `rekeyRisk: false` (`write.ts:580`).
- `flash.ts:437` is in `prepareImage`, which begins with `requireCapability(state.profile, 'flash')` (`flash.ts:120`). `compact-2016` declares flash unsupported (`profiles/compact-2016.ts:120`), so `prepareImage` refuses the profile before line 437.
- So neither site computes a rekey risk on 2016. `footerOk` is false there (the flash has no footer, 42.43 section 3), but that is not what keeps the warning off.

Should it fire on 2016? No. [inferred]
- It states a demonstrated fact: the bank is not bootable. On 2016 every accepting bank is `bootability: 'unknown'`, because no key table matches (`device-info.ts`, the `unknown` branch; 42.43 section 3, 42.48 section 3). Using `checksFooter` in place of `footerOk` would not make the fact true: `!bootable` alone would name every 2016 bank that accepts, a false warning.
- The 2016 write does not re-key: a bank written with its own image reads back byte-identical (the comment at `write.ts:577`).
- So there is no 2016 rule. The comments at `write.ts:565` and `flash.ts:437` say why. Revisit when a 2016 key table can establish "not bootable" (42.48 section 3).

Tests (new; they pass on the unchanged logic).
- `write.test.ts`, "the rekey warning on the 4.x line": a footered, accepting, not-bootable target gets the warning, and the same target without its footer does not. This pins the 4.x rule the comment relies on.
- `write.test.ts`, "the rekey warning never fires on the 2016 line": a 2016 bank that accepts, with `footerOk` true and `bootability: 'unknown'`, gets no warning, and its staging is `slot-keystream-ciphertext`.
- `workflows.test.ts`, "refuses the 2016 profile at its flash capability": `prepareImage` on a compact-2016 state refuses with `profile/unsupported`, before any rekey test.

**1. The active-slot cell and the 2014 "last start" word (plan item 1).**

Each factory image was booted cold on the emulator with the boot-config word at 0x14010000 set to 0, 1 and 2, with fast-forward off, and the machine was kept running after enumeration (42.43's probe stops when the host script ends, which is at enumeration on the 2014 chain). The bank the bootloader entered is the value it stores at 0x10000208 before the hand-off, and the flash reads per bank confirm it. [measured]

| image (boot) | word | bank entered (bootloader store to 0x10000208) | writes to 0x1000AED0 | cell after run | selector 10, +8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.3.0.0 factory dump 101310HSNEA2 | 0 | A (store 0, PC 0x140004E6) | 2 stores from a copy loop, PC 0x10089AF4, values 0x192D1D36 and 0x1933182F | 0x182F192D | 0 |
| same | 1 | A: B is erased, its check fails, A runs (store 0, PC 0x140004E6) | same | 0x182F192D | 0 |
| same | 2 | R (store 2, PC 0x14000544) | same | 0x182F192D | 2 |
| 1.3.0.0 dump with bank B copied from A (a test image, not a factory image) | 1 | B (store 1, PC 0x1400053C) | same | 0x182F192D | 1 |
| 1.3.0.8 image on the 1.3.0.0 donor (the spec's chimera, 1.3.0.0 bootloader) | 0 / 1 / 2 | A / A (B empty) / R | 1 copy store, PC 0x100893CC, value 0x1A001CB1 | 0x1A001CB1 | 0 / 0 / 2 |
| 1.0.3.0 factory dump 0C21A1M5KP15 (2016) | 0 / 1 / 2 | A / B / R (stores 0 at PC 0x140004F6; 1 and 2 at PC 0x140003FE; the flash reads are of B for 1 and of R for 2) | 1 copy store, PC 0x10089C76, value 0x8B8A8C8D | 0x8B8A8C8D | 0 / 1 / 2 |

- No factory image stores a slot value to 0x1000AED0. The only stores are copy loops in the app's startup (the PCs above) that write non-slot words, and the cell keeps the last one. None of the three factory images contains the literal 0x1000AED0 or 0x1000AEC8 (a literal scan of the 47,768, 49,128 and 51,848-byte images; Thumb code names an absolute address through a literal word). [measured]
- Selector 10 returns the boot record at 0x10000200. Its first word is the blank-info pointer (0x14002AB8 on 1.3.0.0, 0x14002958 on 2016), its second is 0x14010000, and its active-slot word is at +8 (0x10000208). The bootloader writes that word before it enters the image: the 2014 `startup.c:142-149` writes 0 for 0x14050000, 1 for 0x14060000 and 2 otherwise, and the 2016 `startup.c:187-194` does the same. The stores in the table are those lines. [measured; source]
- So the 2014 display reads the word the bootloader wrote for the bank it entered. On the emulator the mapping in `boot-choice.ts` (0 is A, 1 is B, 2 is R) matches all three banks, and A is distinct from "not written" because the bootloader writes the 0 explicitly. The line is supported by this measurement, not unreliable. [measured]
- The premise is wrong. `boot-choice.ts:8-12` says the word "is the app's RAM cell 0x1000AED0, not the bootloader's handoff". For this build both parts are wrong. The 2016 bootloader also records the bank it entered (1 for B, 2 for R), which contradicts the file's statement that the word is "not established as a boot record" on that line. `bootChoiceOf` still reports nothing there, which stays the conservative choice.

Recommended, not changed: correct `boot-choice.ts:8-12` to name 0x10000208 and the bootloader's store, and cite the rows above. Whether the 2016 line should show the word is the owner's call.

Caveats: the 1.3.0.8 rows run on the 1.3.0.0 bootloader (the chimera), so they test the record path, not the 1.3.0.8 bootloader. Nothing was read from a camera. The 4.x findings (42.43, 42.50) are not affected.

**2. The FF platforms' bank maps (plan item 3).**

Each platform's bootloader is identified by its build date and the tree whose `bootloader.h` or `image.c` carries that date. The FF 1.3.0.8 camera reports 2.0.2.3 "Jul  5 2018" (42.11b), which is the Compact XR tree. [source] Each map is checked against the corpus dumps that carry the same bootloader (slot lists in `data/corpus/MANIFEST.json`). [measured]

| FF platform | bootloader (build, tree) | A | B | R | boot word | select code (source) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compact FF 1.3.0.8 (16 Hz) | 2.0.2.3, Jul 5 2018 (`compact_xr_bootloader`) | 0x14030000 | 0x14050000 | 0x14070000 | 0x14010000 | `select_boot_slot` (`boot_main.c:129-244`): 0 or 0xFFFFFFFF gives A, B, R; 1 gives B, A, R; any other value gives R, A, B |
| Compact PRO FF 1.0.3.x | Jun 26 2016 (`compact_pro_ff_18hz_1_0_3_0_bootloader`) | 0x14050000 | 0x14060000 | 0x14070000 | 0x14010000 | `boot_select_image` (`image.c:1076-1105`): the same rule |
| Compact PRO FF 4.18.2.0 | Jan 7 2019 (`compact_pro_ff_bootloader`) | 0x14030000 | 0x14050000 | 0x14070000 | 0x14010000 | `select_boot_slot` (`boot_main.c:189`); not read in full |
| Mosaic FF 2.27.1.33 | Jan 7 2019 (`mosaic_ff_bootloader`) | 0x14030000 | 0x14050000 | 0x14070000 | 0x14010000 | not read |

- 1.3.0.8 FF: `bootloader.h:21-25` in the XR tree. The Compact XR 4.8.2.1 dump has the same bootloader build (Jul 5 2018) and holds images at 0x14030000, 0x14050000 and 0x14070000. The 42.11b FF dump holds the same three. The corpus has no full dump of 1.3.0.8 FF.
- PRO FF 1.0.3.x: `image.c:1064-1066`. Dump 0B14A1JULD54 holds images at 0x14050000, 0x14060000 and 0x14070000; dump 1C1AB1CBC8A3 holds one, at 0x14070000.
- PRO FF 4.18.2.0: `bootloader.h:23-25`. The three 4.18.2.0 FF dumps hold images at 0x14030000, 0x14050000 and 0x14070000, with boot word 0.

The runner and build tables on `plan-hygiene` (`752378ea3`; read, not edited) agree with these maps:
- `targets/compact_ff_16hz_1_3_0_8/tools/jlink/jlink-runner.js:54` SLOT_BASES {0x14030000, 0x14050000, 0x14070000}, and `tools/build_flash.mjs:45-47`: correct.
- `targets/compact_pro_ff_18hz_1_0_3_0/tools/jlink/jlink-runner.js:54-58` BANK_BASES {A 0x14050000, B 0x14060000, R 0x14070000}, and `tools/build_flash.mjs:48-51`: correct.
- `targets/compact_pro_ff_18hz_4_18_2_0/tools/build_flash.mjs` SLOTS a 0x14030000, b 0x14050000, recovery 0x14070000: correct.

So the 42.40 choices stand: the 2014-chain table for the PRO FF 1.0.3.x runners and the 4.x table for the 1.3.0.8 FF runner. The plan's "no file states either platform's map" is wrong; `bootloader.h` and `image.c` state both. No fix is needed.

Quirk (source): the XR tree's hand-off writes slot word 0 for A and 2 for every other bank (`boot_main.c:522-524`), so on the 2.0.2.3 platform a start from B and a start from R look the same to selector 10. Not measured here.

Not measured: the 2.0.2.3 bank selection on the emulator. The Compact XR 4.8.2.1 dump (bootloader Jul 5 2018) booted with words 0, 1 and 2, but the flash-window hook saw no bank reads, and the word at 0x10000208 held 0x292A7D70 (neither 0 nor 2). That run is not explained, and nothing above depends on it.

**3. The 1.3.0.8 stalls and the FF patch in the spec (plan item 2).**

`seek-fps-emulator.e2e` was run on FW-V1 `emu-sensor` (`08e1abc6e`, which has `--flash-entry` for the patched boots). The failures reproduce: 8 of 15 passed, 7 failed. After the change: 14 passed, 1 skipped (the FF patched test, by design).

(a) The 1.3.0.8-FF patched test. The throw is `applyFpsPatch` (`fps-patch.ts:329-333`): the stock bank does not hash to the table's `stockSha256`. [measured]
- The table's stock sha for 1.3.0.8-FF is `b97ced91…`, which is the sha of the plain decrypted image in the corpus. For 1.3.0.8 (non-FF) it is `2969d0df…`, the corpus image's sha, and the patched 1.3.0.8 boot works.
- The FF stock bank the emulator writes (`seek-fps-truth-compact_32k-1.3.0.8-FF-to32.bin`, bank 0x14050000, 64 KiB) hashes to `32af77ed…`. Its image region does not match the plain image (the first 16 bytes are `732db02a…` against `00800110…`). Bank R holds the same bytes. The 42.11b camera's bank R hashes to `32af77ed…`, so the emulator stores the FF image as the camera does: encrypted, with only the header at +0x200 in the clear.
- So the test uses the right bank (the FF image is in the chimera's A and R, and B is erased), but `patch-images.ts` assumes a plain-stored bank, as its own header says. This build cannot be patched by that path. Harness fix: `patchable: false` for 1.3.0.8-FF, and a `NOT_BUILT` line.

(b) The 0x56 stalls (1.3.0.8 at 8 Hz and FF; FastRaw, Raw and IP 6).
- 0x56 is SetShutterPolarity, with the record flag `RPC_MODE0_IDLE` (`rpc_cmds.c:4063`). The set dispatcher `rpc_dispatch_set_byid` (`rpc_cmds.c:3524-3600`) refuses a request whose record lacks the flag for the current operation mode, and the refusal status is `mode | 0x30000`. A non-zero dispatch result stalls EP0 (`usb_core.c:2385-2390`). Measured: GetErrorCode (vendor IN 0x35) after the 0x56 stall reads 0x30001, which is operation mode 1 (RUN). [measured]
- Why RUN: the connect ends with SetOperationMode(1) (the checker's `sendInit`). On this build the only operation-0 write before the init is 0x37, "Startup with Operation=0", and the build refuses it, so the option is off. The checker's `reinit` calls `stopStreaming()` before `sendInit`, and `sendInit` sends its three SetOperationMode(0) only `if (this.streaming)`, so the reinit never reaches operation 0. The Swift `reinit` has the same order (`Camera.swift:192-196`, with the check at `:146-151`). [source]
- Replay on the emulator (connect, then reinit): without an operation-0 write, the 0x56 stalls with 0x30001. With three SetOperationMode(0) first, 0x56 is served, SetIPMode(0) and (8) are served, and SetIPMode(3) and (6) stall on 0x3E. [measured] The SetIPMode mask is `(1 << mode) & 0x391`, so the legal modes are 0, 4, 7, 8 and 9 (`rpc_cmds.c:903-935` and the `cmd_SetIPMode` handler; the FF build has the same mask). FastRaw (3) and IP 6 cannot stream on these builds, whatever the entry. Raw (0) can.
- Spec change (commit `2bc1b07`): on builds with `startupOpZero: false`, a non-Normal mode switch is preceded by three SetOperationMode(0) writes (the stop the checker's `sendInit` makes while streaming). On 1.3.0.8 the spec expects the 0x3E refusal for FastRaw and IP 6, and expects Raw to stream. The checker is unchanged, because its reinit order is the Swift one.
- Results. 1.3.0.8 (8 Hz): Normal 8.06 fps (28 frames), Raw 8.06 fps (40 frames), FastRaw and IP 6 `control OUT 0x3e -> stall`, patched Normal 32.26 fps (113 frames). 1.3.0.8-FF: Normal 16.13 fps (57 frames), Raw 8.06 fps (40 frames), FastRaw and IP 6 refused at 0x3E. 1.3.0.0, unchanged: FastRaw 32.26 fps, Raw 8.06, IP 6 8.06, patched 32.26.

(c) The link to 42.41 and the 42.37 camera stalls (not measured here). The emulator's stall is the RUN gate, and it is visible in the status a camera can be asked for. A 0x56 stall followed by GetErrorCode gives 0x30001 for RUN. The set path's FW-init check (`g_systick_state_r32k <= 7`) gives 0x30500 ("Request sent during FW init") with the same STALL. A camera left in RUN by a CLI write would stall the same way, and a power cycle would clear it. Reading 0x35 after the stall on the bench would decide which gate it was. [inferred]

- Byte search (`search_capture.py` in the scratchpad) for the known steps. The 1.3.0.0 steady block `84 08 | 59 20 69 20 69 20 79 27` is found at 0xB898, so the search works. The 2014 steps, the 2016 row-14 steps and the 1.3.0.8 steps are absent from the 0.3.0.1 image; its only `84 08` is inside code at file 0x9431. [measured] This does not cover the 0.3.0.1 step encoding, which may differ.
- The reconstruction places its sequencer at 0x1000A228 (`targets/compact_8hz_0_3_0_1/src/data_unattributed.c:546`: 28 rows of 54 bytes, the 4.18.2.0 shape). No word equal to 0x1000A200, 0x1000A218, 0x1000A220, 0x1000A228 or 0x1000A7DA appears anywhere in the 61,132-byte image. So the factory code does not name that table by an absolute address. [measured]

[inferred] The decisive run was not done: boot 0.3.0.1 on the emulator with mode 8 streaming (its Normal baseline is 8.065 Hz, `framerate_tests.py`) and log every store into the candidate RAM. Bytes that appear only in RAM would show the run-time build.

### 42.55 The checker picks its init from a trusted firmware reply and stops the operation-0 stall, mode 4 frames are counted, and the CLI and the slots page say the camera stays unlocked until a power cycle (fakes and emulator only, 2026-10-19)

**Summary.** The five items of `plan.md` section 2 (42.41's checker stall, 42.53's operation-0 gap, 42.54's mode-4 drop, the power-cycle notice, and the re-lock search). No camera, J-Link or USB switch was used. Code: commit `0be89d3` (checker, core, CLI, page, tests); this section is the commit after it. The emulator spec was run only for the 1.3.0.8 rows.

- **1. Init choice (`e2e/lib/bench/seek-fps/camera.ts:148`, `readTrustedFirmware`).** GetFirmwareInfo (8 bytes) is read until two consecutive replies agree on bytes 0 to 3 and the major is 0 to 9, for up to `FIRMWARE_INFO_READS` = 26 reads, 20 ms apart. Core's `readRunningFirmware` was not used: it takes the second reply without asking that the two agree, it reads 36 bytes where the checker has read 8, and it applies no major check, so an unlocked camera's window reply (`b8 2a 00 14`, major 184) would read as a version. The 26-read window is core's own start-up window (500 ms): the first version of the reader used six reads, and the emulator's 1.3.0.8 stock rows failed on "no answer" for the first five, so the window was widened. A reply that is not trusted stops a Compact's connect before any init is sent (`camera.ts:194`, `untrustedFirmwareMessage`). A Pro's init does not depend on the version, so a Pro connects with its firmware shown as `-`. A refused init during connect is reported with `refusedInitMessage` (`camera.ts:203`), which says the camera is unlocked until a power cycle.
- **2. Operation 0 (`camera.ts:438`, `startupOpZeroUsable`; `sendInit`, `leftInRun`, line 447).** On a classic build that takes no Startup with Operation=0 (the option is off, or the build refused it), every init after the first sends three `SetOperationMode(0)` before the init. Before this change the zero writes were sent only while streaming, and `reinit` stops the stream before it calls `sendInit`, so they were never sent (42.53). A `0x37` refusal at connect is caught (`camera.ts:491`, `startupOpZeroRefused`); the connect goes on without it and `info` says so. The shim in `e2e/seek-fps-emulator.e2e.ts` (the `if (!options.startupOpZero …)` block in `measureBoot`) is removed: the checker now does the stop itself.
- **3. Mode 4 (`camera.ts:72` `SEEK_MODE.mode4`; `grabFrame`, line 557; `grabVisualFrame`, line 586; `cli.ts:98`, `--mode 4`).** The status is byte 20 (halfword 10, the frame type), and the switch in `grabVisualFrame` sent status 0 to `default`, which discards the frame without a count, so mode 4 published nothing. FW-V1 `docs/FRAME_RATE_MODES.md` (branch `emu-research`) says the 1.3.0.8 and 4.8.x publish gate skips the header write for mode 4 (`app_init.c:820`, `frame_mode_gate_r32k != 4`), and the emulator still writes type 3 anyway. A camera that skips the write sends status 0 on mode 4, which is what 42.54 reports; the bench measurement is 42.54's, not this section's. Now every status-0 frame is counted in `untypedFrames`, and in mode 4 a status-0 frame is treated as a picture (status 3). The `--fps` and `stream` output say how many there were.
- **4. Power-cycle note.** `SeekDevice.unlockTokenAccepted` (`packages/core/src/protocol/client.ts:97`) is set by `noteBeginAccepted` (line 131) after an 18-byte BeginFirmwareUpgrade is accepted (`armWindow`, line 251, and the selector sweep, `packages/core/src/workflows/sweep.ts:184`). It is not set on a refused token: the fake's wrong-token refusal arrives through the error code, so it is set after that check, not on the write. `UNLOCK_POWER_CYCLE_NOTE` (`legacy-auth.ts:153`) is the one line. The CLI prints it once when a session that sent the token closes (`packages/cli/src/commands/shared.ts:144`, in `openSession`), so `info`, `dump`, `slots` and `preserve` all get it. `info` sends the token by default, through the identify probe (`identifyCamera`, step 3), unless `--profile` or `--no-probe` is given. The page's slots read, dump, write and patch show it through an `Alert` in `SlotsView` (`packages/web/src/views/SlotsView.tsx:64`, `UnlockNote`); the flag is `unlockNote` in `useSlotsPanel.ts:448`, cleared when the camera changes. It is information only and gates nothing.
- **5. Re-lock search (FW-V1, read only).** No request in the 1.3.0.8 RPC table (wires 0x50 to 0x5A, `targets/compact_8hz_1_3_0_8/src/rpc_cmds.c:4038` to 4336) re-locks the window. Candidates checked: 0x59 `ResetDevice` calls `system_reset` (`cmd_ResetDevice`, line 902): a reboot, which clears RAM, and not a re-lock; the checker never sends it, and it is not added. 0x55 `SetFirmwareInfoFeatures` latches the GetFirmwareInfo selector (`docs/EMULATOR_CORPUS.md:3851`, "selectors 0..9 (latched by 85)"); a selector left set would explain window bytes in the GetFirmwareInfo reply, but that is an unverified inference, and 0x55 is itself refused in the stalled state (42.41). `BeginFirmwareUpgrade` takes a power vote (`power_vote_active`, `clocks.c:333`), released by the window-completion paths: power management, not a lock. The 1.3.0.0 handlers (`cmd_BeginFirmwareUpgrade`, `cmd_ResetDevice`) have the same names; its RPC table was not enumerated. Conclusion: no re-lock request is clear in the source, so none is added. A recommendation only: a bench test of a 0x55 selector reset (`SetFirmwareInfoFeatures` 0) after a window-byte reply, and of a 0x59 reset, each on a bench that is allowed to be reset.
